text:
mia: Hey, hitting x509: certificate signed by unknown authority when our Go SDK runs in the container behind corp proxy. Works locally. Anyone seen this with static Go builds?
sam: yup. likely the container doesn't have the corp CA in the system bundle or Go's SystemCertPool is returning nil (musl / CGO disabled).
mia: we're using a scratch-based builder, CGO disabled to keep binary static. alpine base stage. :grimacing:
alex: scratch + musl + CGO disabled = SystemCertPool often empty. Go falls back to an empty pool meaning only root certs you provide will be trusted.
jordan: quick check: does /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt exist in your runtime image? If not, nothing for the binary to use.
mia: runtime is scratch so no files. What's the sane fix? mount CA file? set env var?
sam: common fixes:
- include the distro ca bundle in final image (copy /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt into image)
- set SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR to point at a bundle you ship
- programmatically load a CA file with crypto/x509 and set tls.Config.RootCAs

alex: example snippet to load a bundle in Go:

```
caCertPool := x509.NewCertPool()
bs, err := os.ReadFile("/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")
if err != nil { log.Fatalf("read CA bundle: %v", err) }
if !caCertPool.AppendCertsFromPEM(bs) { log.Fatalf("failed to append CA certs") }
tr := &http.Transport{ TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{ RootCAs: caCertPool } }
client := &http.Client{ Transport: tr }
```

mia: ok that would work but I wanted minimal changes. Can we just set SSL_CERT_FILE in Dockerfile and mount the corp CA from CI?
jordan: yes that'll work for many libraries. For Go, env vars won't change crypto/x509.SystemCertPool behavior if it's empty; but you can point your code to the file or set the system bundle in the image.
sam: another option: enable CGO in the build so SystemCertPool hooks into the OS store (if using glibc). But on scratch static builds that's not an option.
mia: CI can inject /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt at image build time. Any tips to avoid breaking other apps?
alex: ensure the file is the concatenation of distro bundle + corp CA. E.g., in build stage:

```
RUN cp /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /tmp/bundle && cat /corp-ca.pem >> /tmp/bundle && \
    mkdir -p /etc/ssl/certs && cp /tmp/bundle /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```

mia: thanks. One more thing: streaming endpoints sporadically drop with TLS handshake error after ~30s. Could this be related to the proxy cert rotation?
jordan: possibly. If proxy injects certs and rotates them, long-lived HTTP/2 streams can fail on rehandshake or proxy idle timeouts. Check proxy logs and keepalive settings.
sam: set Transport.IdleConnTimeout and TLS handshake timeouts, also ensure HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 behavior. Some corp proxies don't like h2 and do odd buffering.
alex: for debugging locally, curl with --http2 -v --cacert /path/to/corp-ca.pem to see ALPN and handshake. Also strace the container to confirm file presence.
mia: awesome — mounting the bundle + adding the corp CA and adjusting transport timeouts. I'll try that and ping back. Thanks :raised_hands:
devops-bot: Note: if you need the corp CA, open a ticket with infra to add the CA image-safe copy in our artifacts repo.
mia: filing ticket now, thanks.
